item.title: The four-layer memory stack, and the dreaming loop beside it: reading Anthropic's memory research
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: memory is not a transcript you keep, it is cargo moved between four layers — the low ones are true and hard to use, the top one is easy and easy to get wrong. Dreaming is the worker that moves it while nobody is watching. Note on figures: the diagrams here are redrawn from the article’s own data and structure; its fifteen-odd figures and screenshots are at the source linked at the end.

item.title: Seven layers between the model and the result: reading the guide against its own evidence
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. Abstract. Most production agent failures do not happen in the model layer. Split the distance from model to result into seven layers — model, instructions and context, tools, memory, loop, evals and guardrails, human signature — and the most common reflex (swap the model, rewrite the prompt) acts on the one layer least likely to be broken.

item.title: Reading DSec section by section: what a 3-million-sandbox-a-day platform says about agent training
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: the contribution is not another sandbox runtime. It is a measurement of what agent-training sandboxes actually look like — requests arrive in tens of thousands, CPU usage sits at 5% of what was requested, state lives for minutes to hours, and images are barely reused. Once all four hold, the platform cannot be a container runtime; it has to be an elastic execution platform.

item.title: Open Responses: one contract instead of N×M adapters
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: it swaps “messages” for bidirectional items, swaps token streaming for state-machine events, and gives extensions a namespaced side channel — so the endpoint and model name become configuration, and the cost moves from adapters to the semantics of individual fields. Read from three places: the specification itself (both the 2026-01-15 and 2026-04-24 versions), its TypeSpec schema and repository, and the docs of two live implementations at Databricks and Vercel.

item.title: Think Before You Act: How JevAct Gates LLM Agent Actions
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 This English page stays available at its own URL. The Chinese version is the one maintained first. English readers land here directly. To pin English after switching languages, use ?lang=en on this URL, e.g. this link. An agent’s action should pass through a gate that can check, compute, and send back before anything executes. JevAct splits that gate in two. code settles what tool records decide, a decision model answers only “what did the conversation actually say”, and a boolean rule combines them.
